title: ServeGraph: incremental rollout graph with rollback simulator and SLA enforcer
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: unify staged model rollouts with a deterministic simulation pass that verifies rollback behavior and SLA invariants before any traffic promotion. This PR introduces ServeGraph, a lightweight graph representation of incremental rollout stages and transitions plus a rollback simulator that can run against historical traces and live shadow traffic to surface dangerous promotion paths early.

High-level goals: aggregate canaries and A/B branches into a single ServeGraph representation; provide an offline 'simulate-rollback' mode to validate that automatic rollback playbooks will terminate and re-stabilize; enforce SLA gates at each graph edge; persist annotated runbooks to the rollout metadata so operators and the console can show the exact rollback steps taken.

What this changes (summary):
- New data model: rollout_graph_v2 stored in the control-plane Postgres table with lightweight transition annotations (safety_gate, rollback_playbook_ref, cohort_selector). Backwards-compatible migration included.
- Rollout executor: graph-walker component that advances nodes using the existing rollout engine but with deterministic replay hooks to allow simulation.
- Rollback simulator: a new binary (pkg/rollout/simulator) that accepts traces or a live shadow feed and emits a finite-state trace of promotions+rollbacks plus reasons (latency breaches, error spike, quality regressions).
- SLA enforcer: pluggable policy that evaluates per-node SLOs (p99 latency, error-rate, quality-regression) and marks transitions as blocked/unblockable.
- Console + API: new endpoints (POST /rollouts/:id/simulate, GET /rollouts/:id/graph) and a small console UI panel showing simulated paths and annotated runbook steps.
- Tests & docs: integration tests that run simulator against recorded traces and a new docs page describing graph semantics and operator guidance.

Checklist: 
- [x] Data migration with reversible steps
- [x] Simulator runs in CI against synthetic traces
- [x] End-to-end test covering a promoted canary that triggers an automated rollback
- [x] Console rendering of simulation results

Compatibility and risk: designed to be opt-in. Existing linear canary flows map to a simple two-node ServeGraph and behave unchanged unless the new simulation API is called. There is a DB migration but it is non-destructive and reversible by rolling back the feature flag. The rollout executor falls back to the legacy code-path when ServeGraph is disabled.

Why this is useful: teams often discover that automated rollback playbooks have non-terminating or unsafe sequences only after several partial promotions. Running a deterministic simulation against historical traces and shadow traffic reduces blast radius by uncovering promotion paths that would oscillate or violate SLAs. The annotated runbooks make post-incident analysis deterministic and actionable.

Notes on operation: the simulator is intentionally rate-limited in hosted to avoid load on the control plane; customers on Dedicated can enable full-fidelity simulation against private traces. The default safety gates are conservative and will block promotions if p99 or error-rate regressions are observed in the simulation run.
commits: Init ServeGraph schema and migration; add graph walker and deterministic hooks; implement rollback simulator binary; add API endpoints and console panel; integration tests and docs; fix race in executor; add feature flag and rollout to canary infra
review_comments:
Marcus: please split the big migration into smaller, reviewable steps; Diego: simulator looks good but add a timeout and defensive checks for malformed traces; Priya: add more console unit tests and an integration that asserts the runbook annotations are displayed.

Author replies: split migration into two statements (schema then backfill) and added feature flag gating; added simulator timeout with graceful cancel; added two console unit tests and one integration asserting runbook->UI mapping.

Final review: Marcus approved after minor nits; Diego approved after simulator timeout fix; Priya approved after tests added. CI was green after re-run (one flaky e2e was re-run and passed).
release_notes: ServeGraph rollout graph and rollback simulator: adds a new graph-based rollout model with an offline simulator to validate automatic rollback playbooks and enforce per-stage SLAs. Opt-in feature behind a feature-flag; includes a reversible DB migration and console support.
notes: Deployed to canary tier 2026-02-20; monitoring dashboard added under Rollouts -> Simulations; on-call runbook updated to include simulation as a pre-promotion step.
